summary: The DME Scammer Prevention Act of 2026 establishes new billing requirements under Medicare for certain durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics, and supplies that are on a specific Master List. It requires claims for these items to be filed electronically and within 90 days of when they are furnished, starting January 1, 2027. Additionally, it directs the Government Accountability Office to report on the technology used by Medicare administrative contractors to identify fraudulent claims.

affected_groups.effect: Must submit claims electronically and within 90 days for specified medical equipment and supplies on the Master List.
Must complete and submit a report to Congress by January 1, 2030, regarding claim screening technology and denied claims.

key_provisions: Requires all providers and suppliers to submit claims electronically for specified medical equipment and supplies included on the Medicare Master List furnished on or after January 1, 2027.

Requires claims for applicable items to be filed within 90 days of the date of service, with certain exceptions such as items on specific face-to-face encounter lists, prior authorization lists, or items paid on a monthly rental basis.

Mandates that the Comptroller General of the United States submit a report to Congress by January 1, 2030, on the technology used by Medicare administrative contractors to screen claims for specified items.
Requires the 2030 report to examine the total number of claims initially denied by screening technology and those ultimately paid for a one-year period beginning January 1, 2027.

The specific details of what technology Medicare administrative contractors currently use beyond what is evaluated in the future report.

It requires claims for these items to be filed electronically and within 90 days of when they are furnished, starting January 1, 2027. Additionally, it directs the Government Accountability Office to report on the technology used by Medicare administrative contractors to identify fraudulent claims.
summary_detail.significance: The bill aims to promote program integrity and address fiscal vulnerabilities within Medicare for certain durable medical equipment and supplies by tightening billing timeframes and mandating electronic submission and technology evaluations.
